title: Preimage of a singleton under the special-bit flip
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$, and let $\phi$ be the map on hard samples that flips only Alice's special-coordinate bit, sending a sample $\omega = (T, x_T, y_T, \mathrm{other})$ to $(T, \lnot x_T, y_T, \mathrm{other})$. Then for every hard sample $\omega$, the preimage of the singleton $\{\omega\}$ under $\phi$ is exactly the singleton $\{\phi(\omega)\}$; that is, $\phi^{-1}(\{\omega\}) = \{\phi(\omega)\}$.
